description: Signature edition. overview: In the Signature teaching of compilers, What Compilers Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Lexical analysis means scanning source characters into tokens, the words of the language. Intermediate representation means a portable, optimizable form like LLVM IR between front end and back end. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Lexical analysis: scanning source characters into tokens, the words of the language.
Intermediate representation: a portable, optimizable form like LLVM IR between front end and back end.
key_laws: Chomsky hierarchy: regular, context-free, and richer grammars matching lexers, parsers, and beyond.
vocabulary: Token: the smallest meaningful unit a lexer emits, like a number or keyword.
Grammar: the formal rules defining which token sequences are valid programs.
methods: Grammar design: writing unambiguous grammars that parse efficiently.

overview: In the Signature teaching of compilers, Building optimization passes is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary.
